title: Callback chain broken in unexpected way with combination of association + callbacks
body:
This is related to #36082 in that the issue we're seeing in the GitHub application is caused by the same commit but I think we have discovered some buggy behavior.

In our application we have some models that have a corresponding "archived" table so we can "delete" records and their associations without having to actually delete them. We do a replace into the archived table and then delete from the original table. There are reasons we do this, and I could get into why, but I can demonstrate an unexpected change in behavior in Rails due to #36082 in the callback chain without explaining why we do that in our app.

In our case we have models that have `after_commit on: :destroy` callbacks that we use to loop through and throttle the deletion of records. For large repositories this is really important for us.

Since updating Rails last week we've had a few test failures we're working through, one is showing our `after_commit` callbacks are **not** firing at all on destroy for our archive code. I've reproduced the issue outside of our app in the script below. In order to reproduce the issue a few things must be true:

1) A model (Post) has a `has_many` association (Comment) that is `dependent: :destroy` and a lambda adding an order (I don't know why but the lambda is required to repro this, it could be empty, or where or whatever but the lambda is one part of reproducing this).
2) The `has_many` model (Comment) belongs to Post, and has an `after_destroy` callback that updates the Post record. In our app we use this to update the number of downloads before a repo is deleted. A `before_destroy` callback also breaks the chain if it also updates the Post.

With this scenario any callbacks that are `after_commit on: :destroy` on the Post model will NOT be called and will be completely skipped. If I change this to an `after_destroy` it works fine.

Our code may not be the best pattern here but my main concern is how hard it was to figure out what broke and am wary that this will break other apps in unexpected ways.

I've created a reproduction script that demonstrates the issue but doesn't represent a real world case. The script shows how the `after_commit` callback is never fired by using an array to capture that it was fired.

This test passes before https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/35920 was introduced and fails afterwards. Here's the script

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "active_record"
require "minitest/autorun"
require "logger"

# This connection will do for database-independent bug reports.
ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: "sqlite3", database: ":memory:")
ActiveRecord::Base.logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :posts, force: true do |t| 
    t.string :title
  end 

  create_table :comments, force: true do |t| 
    t.text :comment_body
    t.integer :post_id
  end 
end

class Post < ActiveRecord::Base
  # This never gets called when order and an after_destroy
  # callback that updates Post is called
  #
  # This also works if we use `after_destroy`. I think what happens here is that
  # when we made after_commit not fire for if a record isn’t saved Rails is
  # considering this record not saved.
  after_commit on: :destroy do
    self.callback_called << "yes"
  end

  # if we don’t have a lamdba OR don’t have a callback on comment this passes
  has_many :comments, -> { order("comments.id DESC") }, dependent: :destroy

  def callback_called
    @callback_called ||= []
  end

  def callback_called=(callback_called)
    @callback_called = [callback_called]
  end
end

class Comment < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :post

  # Remove this and Post’s after_commit callbacks will be called.
  after_destroy :save_post

  # This must update/save a comment to break the callback chain
  def save_post
    post.save!
  end
end

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_after_commit
    post = Post.create!(title: "I am a post")
    comment = post.comments.create(comment_body: "i am a comment")

    assert_equal 1, post.comments.count

    post.destroy

    # pass - post is successfully deleted
    assert !Post.exists?(post.id)
    # pass - comments are successfully deleted
    assert_equal 0, Comment.where(post_id: post.id).count
    # fail - callbacks are not called when order, dependency, and an after_destroy
    # callback is used.
    assert_equal ["yes"], post.callback_called
  end
end
```

@kamipo I'd like you to weigh in on whether this behavior is expected or not with the change you made to `after_commit`

cc/ @jhawthorn @tenderlove @cpruitt for visibility.
